title: Throughput Governor: Constraint Synthesizer for Autoscaling Policies
creator: Anika Shah
description: Build a 'Throughput Governor' component that synthesizes safe, workload-aware constraints for the autoscaling engine used by Dedicated capacity. This component translates high-level throughput guarantees and business constraints into concrete scaling parameters (target metrics, step sizes, cooldowns, and budget guards) per fleet and per-tenant. The goal is to enable predictable throughput guarantees while preventing oscillation and runaway scale-ups that increase cost or impact colocated tenants.
acceptance_criteria: CI: Throughput Governor produces a policy bundle for any given fleet that includes: primary target metric, secondary guard metric(s), max step, min replicas, cooldown, budget cap, and emergency fallback policy.

Simulated workloads in staging: governor-generated policies maintain 99th-percentile latency target for stable and bursty workloads with <3x temporary overshoot of replicas and no sustained throttling after 10 minutes.
Operator controls in Console: ability to preview synthesized constraints and override specific parameters for a fleet.
Performance: policy synthesis latency <250ms so runtime/controller can request updates without blocking reconciliation loops.
Auditability: every synthesized policy linked to inputs (SLAs, historical QPS distribution, tenant tier) recorded in audit log with trace ID.
Security: component passes security review for access to tenant metadata and billing caps.
decisions: Design decoupled synthesizer: separate 'policy synthesis' (offline/nearline) from 'policy runtime' (fast evaluation in controller). Rationale: expensive forecasting and heavy-tailed analysis run async; runtime caches results and applies quick guards.
Primary target metric chosen: effective QPS per-GPU normalized to 'tokens-per-second' for text workloads. Secondary guards: GPU utilization 95th, p99 latency, and error-rate spike detector.

Scaling algorithm: default to dual-controller approach - rate-based proportional controller (P-term) with capped ramping and an optional predictive feedforward from short-term ARIMA-like forecast for bursty tenants. Rationale: P-controller simplest, predictable; feedforward helps absorb short bursts without overscale.

Safety limits: max scale factor per minute = 2x (configurable per fleet), max absolute replicas limit from capacity reservation, emergency cost budget gate (monthly committed budget) enforced at admission-time and runtime.
Cooldowns: default 120s between non-emergency scale actions; emergency path can act with 15s cooldown but requires two independent triggers (metric threshold + error-increase).
Fallback policy: if primary model unavailable, fall back to conservative static policy generated from 95th percentile QPS of the last 7 days.
Observability: every decision emits trace events and a 'why' field with contributing signals (e.g., 'p99-latency breached, qps growth +40% 3min').
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (MVP): implement synthesizer as a service that consumes fleet spec + historical metrics and emits policy.json. Expose HTTP API used by autoscale controller.

Policy format: flat JSON with primitive values only (no nested objects) for controller compatibility: primary_metric, primary_target, secondary_metrics (comma-separated), max_step, min_replicas, max_replicas, cooldown_seconds, emergency_budget_threshold, fallback_policy_key.
Workload profiling: use rolling window distributions (10m, 1h, 24h) and compute percentiles for QPS and p95/p99 latency. Use these to pick conservative min_replicas and baseline target.
Forecasting: simple exponential smoothing implementation in Go for low-latency predictions. Keep model state per-fleet in Redis for quick access; recompute full model weekly.
Config surface: fleet.yaml extension to allow admin overrides for max_step, emergency_budget, and target latency bands.
Rate-limits: synth service must authenticate via mTLS and respect RBAC; add Circuit Breaker to serve previous policy when downstream metrics unavailable.
Database: store synthesized policy artifacts in policy-store (Postgres table with trace_id, inputs_hash, created_at, created_by).
test_plan: Unit tests for policy synthesis algorithms and edge-case inputs (e.g., flat zero QPS, extreme spikes).
Integration tests: autoscale controller consumes synthesized policy and performs simulated scaling actions in runtime testbench (we already have harness in infra/tests/autoscale-harness).
Chaos test: inject delayed metrics and partial-controller failures; validate fallback and cooldown enforcement.
Cost safety test: create scenario that would normally request >10x scale; assert emergency_budget gate prevents policy that would exceed configured spend cap.
Performance test: ensure synthesis API returns <250ms for profiles with up to 90 days of historical buckets compressed via sketching.
E2E smoke in staging with 3 tenant tiers: free, standard, enterprise — validate target guarantees and manual override flow through Console.
